title: Create a DataFrame from List
problemStatement: Write a solution to create a DataFrame from a 2D list called `student_data`. The list contains the id and age of some students. The DataFrame must have two columns, `student_id` and `age`, in that order.

title: Drop Duplicate Rows
problemStatement: There are some duplicate rows in the `customers` DataFrame based on the `email` column. Remove the duplicates, keeping only the first occurrence of each email, and return the resulting DataFrame with the original column order preserved.

title: Fill Missing Data
problemStatement: The `products` DataFrame contains missing values in the `quantity` column. Replace every missing quantity with 0 and return the resulting DataFrame.

title: Reshape Data: Melt
problemStatement: The `report` DataFrame holds one column per quarter. Reshape it from wide to long format so that the result has the columns `product`, `quarter` and `sales`, keeping the quarters in their original column order.

title: Monthly Transactions I
problemStatement: Given the `transactions` DataFrame, find for each month and country the number of transactions and their total amount, together with the number of approved transactions and their total amount. The `month` column must be formatted as YYYY-MM.

title: Restaurant Growth
problemStatement: Given the `customer` DataFrame, compute the moving average of how much a restaurant earns over a window of seven days (the current day plus the six days before it). Return `visit_date`, the total `amount` paid in the window, and `average_amount` rounded to two decimals, ordered by `visit_date`. Amounts on the same day must be summed first.

title: Friend Requests II: Who Has the Most Friends
problemStatement: The `request_accepted` DataFrame holds accepted friend requests. Find the person who has the most friends and the number of friends they have. The test data guarantees that exactly one person has the most friends.

title: Count Salary Categories
problemStatement: Given the `accounts` DataFrame, count the number of bank accounts in each salary category: 'Low Salary' for income below 20000, 'Average Salary' for income between 20000 and 50000 inclusive, and 'High Salary' for income above 50000. Every category must appear in the result, with a count of 0 when no account falls into it.

title: Last Person to Fit in the Bus
problemStatement: The `queue` DataFrame describes a boarding queue, where `turn` is the boarding order and `weight` is the person's weight in kilograms. The bus has a weight limit of 1000 kilograms. Find the name of the last person who can board without exceeding the limit. The test data guarantees the first person does not exceed the limit.

title: Product Sales Analysis III
problemStatement: Given the `sales` and `product` DataFrames, report the product id, the first year each product was sold, and the quantity and price of every sale made in that first year. Return the result in any order.

title: Average Time of Process per Machine
problemStatement: The `activity` DataFrame records the start and end timestamp of each process run on each machine. Compute the average processing time of each machine, rounded to three decimal places, where the processing time of a process is its end timestamp minus its start timestamp.

title: Reshape Data: Pivot
problemStatement: The `weather` DataFrame records the monthly temperature of several cities in long format. Pivot it so that each row is a month and each column is a city holding that city's temperature. Return the result with `month` as an ordinary first column rather than an index.

title: Reshape Data: Concatenate
problemStatement: Two DataFrames `df1` and `df2` share the same columns. Concatenate them vertically into a single DataFrame, with the rows of df1 first, and reset the index so it runs from zero.

title: Drop Missing Data
problemStatement: The `students` DataFrame contains rows where the `name` column is missing. Remove those rows and return the remaining students with a reset index.

title: Method Chaining
problemStatement: The `animals` DataFrame holds the name, species, age and weight of several animals. List the names of the animals that weigh strictly more than 100 kilograms, sorted by weight in descending order, returning only the `name` column.

title: Group Sold Products By The Date
problemStatement: Given the `activities` DataFrame, report for each sell date the number of different products sold and a comma-separated string of their names sorted alphabetically. Order the result by sell date.

title: Customers Who Bought All Products
problemStatement: Given the `customer` DataFrame of purchases and the `product` DataFrame of all product keys, report the ids of customers who bought every product in the product table. Return the result in any order.

title: Confirmation Rate
problemStatement: The confirmation rate of a user is the number of confirmed messages divided by the total number of confirmation requests they received, and is zero for users who requested none. Given the `signups` and `confirmations` DataFrames, report the confirmation rate of every user rounded to two decimal places, in any order.

title: Movie Rating
problemStatement: Given the `movies`, `users` and `movie_rating` DataFrames, report two rows in a single column named `results`: first the name of the user who rated the greatest number of movies, then the title of the movie with the highest average rating in February 2020. Ties are broken by the lexicographically smaller name or title.

title: Capital Gain/Loss
problemStatement: The `stocks` DataFrame records Buy and Sell operations for several stocks, where every buy is eventually followed by a sell. Report the capital gain or loss of each stock, that is the total selling price minus the total buying price, in any order.

title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
problemStatement: The `products` DataFrame records whether each product is low fat ('Y'/'N') and recyclable ('Y'/'N'). Find the ids of products that are both low fat and recyclable.

title: Find Customer Referee
problemStatement: The `customer` DataFrame has columns id, name and referee_id, where referee_id may be missing. Find the names of customers who were not referred by the customer with id 2 (including customers with no referee at all).

title: Invalid Tweets
problemStatement: The `tweets` DataFrame has columns tweet_id and content. Find the ids of invalid tweets, defined as tweets whose content is strictly longer than 15 characters.

data: More than fifteen chars are here!

title: Replace Employee ID With The Unique Identifier
problemStatement: The `employees` DataFrame has columns id and name; the `employee_uni` DataFrame maps some of those ids to a unique_id. Show the unique id of each employee in place of their id; employees without a mapped unique_id should show a missing value, and every employee from `employees` must appear exactly once.

title: Calculate Special Bonus
problemStatement: The `employees` DataFrame has columns employee_id, name and salary. Calculate the bonus of every employee: it equals their salary if their employee_id is odd and their name does not start with 'M', otherwise it is 0. Return employee_id and bonus, ordered by employee_id.

title: The Latest Login in 2020
problemStatement: The `logins` DataFrame has columns user_id and time_stamp. Report the latest login time in the year 2020 for each user who logged in during 2020; users with no logins in 2020 must not appear.

title: Employees Whose Manager Left the Company
problemStatement: The `employees` DataFrame has columns employee_id, name, manager_id (nullable) and salary. Find the ids of employees whose salary is strictly less than 30000, who have a manager, and whose manager is no longer present in the employees table. Return the result ordered by employee_id.

title: The Number of Employees Which Report to Each Employee
problemStatement: The `employees` DataFrame has columns employee_id, name, reports_to (nullable) and age. For every employee who has at least one direct report, compute the number of employees reporting to them and the average age of those reports rounded to two decimal places. Return employee_id, name, reports_count and average_age, ordered by employee_id.

title: Nth Highest Salary
problemStatement: The `employee` DataFrame has columns id and salary, and an integer `N` is provided. Return the Nth highest distinct salary in a single-row, single-column DataFrame named `getNthHighestSalary(N)`; if no Nth highest salary exists, the value must be missing.

title: Employee Bonus
problemStatement: The `employee` DataFrame has columns empId, name, supervisor and salary; the `bonus` DataFrame maps some empIds to a bonus amount. Report the name and bonus of every employee whose bonus is missing or strictly less than 1000.

title: Fix Names in a Table
problemStatement: The `users` DataFrame has columns user_id and name, where names may have inconsistent capitalization. Fix every name so only the first letter is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Return the result ordered by user_id.

title: List the Products Ordered in a Period
problemStatement: Given the `products` DataFrame and the `orders` DataFrame, find the name and total ordered quantity of every product that had at least 100 units ordered in February 2020.

title: Tree Node
problemStatement: The `tree` DataFrame represents a tree with columns id and p_id (the parent id, missing for the root). Classify every node's type as 'Root' (no parent), 'Leaf' (no children) or 'Inner' (has both a parent and at least one child).

title: Biggest Single Number
problemStatement: The `my_numbers` DataFrame has a single column `num` which may contain duplicates. Find the largest value that occurs exactly once; report a missing value if no such number exists.

title: Triangle Judgement
problemStatement: The `triangle` DataFrame has columns x, y and z representing three side lengths. For each row, report whether the three sides can form a valid triangle (every pair of sides must sum to more than the third).

title: Daily Leads and Partners
problemStatement: The `daily_sales` DataFrame records sales activity with columns date_id, make_name, lead_id and partner_id. For each distinct (date_id, make_name) pair, report the number of distinct lead_ids and the number of distinct partner_ids.

title: Patients With a Condition
problemStatement: The `patients` DataFrame has columns patient_id, patient_name and conditions, where conditions is a space-separated list of codes. Find every patient who has a Type I Diabetes code, identified by a code that starts with 'DIAB1' (matching only at the start of the string or after a space, not as a substring elsewhere).

title: Game Play Analysis I
problemStatement: The `activity` DataFrame records each login event of a player with columns player_id, device_id, event_date and games_played. For each player, report the date of their first login.

title: Students With Invalid Departments
problemStatement: The `students` DataFrame has columns id, name and department_id; the `departments` DataFrame lists valid department ids. Find every student whose department_id does not correspond to any existing department.
